references.text: The bronze serpent in the wilderness is the direct Old Testament type that Jesus refers to in [ref:Joh 3:14|John 3:14]. Whoever looked at the bronze serpent was healed – a picture of whoever believes in Christ and receives eternal life ([ref:4 Mos 21:8-9|Num 21:8-9]).

[ref:Joh 3:16|John 3:16] expands on and explains verse 15 by showing that it is God’s love that lies behind it: "For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life."

[ref:Joh 3:36|John 3:36] repeats and reinforces the theme of faith and eternal life: "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life." The contrast with the one who does not believe underscores the necessity of faith.

In [ref:Joh 6:40|John 6:40], Jesus says: "For this is my Father’s will, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life." Same pattern: belief in the Son gives eternal life, available to "everyone who" (πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων).
[ref:Joh 6:47|John 6:47]: "Whoever believes has eternal life." Jesus again confirms the central promise from [ref:Joh 3:15|John 3:15] that faith gives eternal life.

In [ref:Joh 11:25-26|John 11:25-26], Jesus declares: "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live … and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never die." Eternal life is directly linked to faith in Jesus.

[ref:Joh 20:31|John 20:31] summarizes the entire purpose of the Gospel of John: "that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name." This is the thematic conclusion to the promise in [ref:Joh 3:15|John 3:15].

[ref:Apg 10:43|Acts 10:43]: "To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name." The expression "everyone who believes" (πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων) is identical to the wording in John 3:15.

[ref:Rom 10:11|Romans 10:11]: "For the Scripture says, Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame." Paul uses the universal promise – "everyone who believes" – which reflects the same truth as in [ref:Joh 3:15|John 3:15].

[ref:1 Joh 5:11-13|1 John 5:11-13] summarizes that "God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life." In his letter, John confirms what he wrote in the Gospel: that eternal life is found in faith in God’s Son.
